title: Brain Infiltrating Leukocytes (BILs) Extraction
author: Alexandra Kazanova
materials: Adjust cell number and proceed to FACS staining.

steps.title: Prepare tubes and reagents
steps.instruction: Label 15 mL conical tubes, add 3 mL RPMI to each, weigh each tube, and set aside all reagents (aCD45‑FITC, digestion enzyme mix, PBS with 2 mM EDTA and 10 % FBS, FACS buffer, Percoll, D‑PBS with Ca/Mg, ACK lysis buffer).

steps.title: Inject mice with antibody
steps.instruction: Inject each mouse intraperitoneally with 200 µL aCD45‑FITC solution.

steps.title: Sacrifice mice at precise time
steps.instruction: Exactly 20 minutes after injection, euthanize each mouse by cervical dislocation.

steps.title: Harvest brain into RPMI on ice
steps.instruction: Using a spatula, place each brain into its pre‑filled 15 mL tube (3 mL RPMI) and keep the tube on ice; weigh the tube to determine brain weight.

steps.title: Mince brain tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the brain to a petri dish and cut it into small pieces with scissors.

steps.title: Return pieces to collection tube
steps.instruction: Using a cut 1 mL pipette tip, collect the minced pieces and transfer them back into the original 15 mL tube containing RPMI.

steps.title: Centrifuge and prepare digestion mix
steps.instruction: Spin the tube at 1500 rpm, 4 °C for 5 minutes; while the tube is spinning, prepare the RT digestion enzyme mix (1×).

steps.title: Add digestion enzyme mix
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL of the RT digestion enzyme mix to the tube and mix gently (vortex if desired).

steps.title: Incubate digestion with intermittent shaking
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 37 °C for 35 minutes, applying gentle shaking at 15‑minute and 30‑minute marks.

steps.title: Neutralize enzymes on ice
steps.instruction: Immediately place the tube on ice and add 5 mL PBS containing 2 mM EDTA and 10 % FBS to stop the digestion.

steps.title: Filter digested tissue through strainer
steps.instruction: Prime a cell strainer (placed on a 50 mL tube) with 10 mL FACS buffer; add the digested brain suspension onto the strainer, flush with an additional 5 mL FACS buffer, then push the remaining material through using a 3 mL syringe plunger while continuously pouring FACS buffer to a final volume of up to 50 mL.

steps.title: Centrifuge cells post‑filtration
steps.instruction: Spin the filtered cell suspension at 300 × g, room temperature, for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Prepare Percoll gradient
steps.instruction: For each brain, mix 3.7 mL Percoll with 5.3 mL D‑PBS (containing calcium and magnesium) to obtain a 10 mL gradient solution.

steps.title: Layer cells onto gradient
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant from the previous spin, gently resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL D‑PBS, and transfer this suspension into a fresh 15 mL tube that already contains 9 mL of the prepared gradient solution (total 10 mL).

steps.title: Gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 500 × g, room temperature, for 20 minutes without brake; ensure the centrifuge is set to RT before starting.

steps.title: Remove myelin upper layer
steps.instruction: Using cut 1 mL pipette tips, carefully collect and discard the upper myelin layer.

steps.title: Wash with ice‑cold PBS
steps.instruction: Add ice‑cold PBS to the top of the tube, then spin at 400 × g, 4 °C, for 5 minutes with brake; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Collect interphase fraction
steps.instruction: Collect the interphase up to the lowest red‑cell‑containing sediment (≈7 mL) and transfer it to a 50 mL tube.

steps.title: Optional RBC lysis if needed
steps.instruction: If red‑cell debris is present, add 1 mL ACK lysis buffer, mix, incubate 30 seconds, then block with 4 mL 10 % FBS in PBS; spin at 400 × g, 4 °C, 5 minutes with brake and discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend final cells and count
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 200 µL FACS buffer, take a small aliquot, stain with trypan blue, and count cells (expect 0.5–1 × 10⁶ cells per UI mouse).
